title: Pairing mechanism of nickelate superconductors
bottleneck: Infinite-layer nickelates superconduct at ambient pressure — up to 44 K in recent rare-earth variants — and are stable in air, unlike cuprates. But the pairing mechanism is unknown: theories invoke pair density waves and unusual flat-band physics that may differ fundamentally from cuprate pairing. Without a confirmed mechanism, researchers cannot rationally design nickelates with higher Tc or better critical currents.
why_it_blocks: Nickelates are the first genuinely new high-Tc family in decades and the most promising lead toward ambient-pressure, higher-temperature superconductivity. Blind synthesis without mechanistic understanding means progress depends on luck rather than design, wasting the opportunity.
current_state: The 2026 SuperC discovery of kagome-lattice superconductors identified via quantum geometry plus machine learning offers a template for mechanism-guided search. For nickelates specifically, the mechanism debate remains open, with the PNAS 2026 agenda listing unconventional pairing as a core research direction.
